Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed opacity that forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall and diaphragm, which is the classic radiographic sign of an extrapulmonary (pleural or chest wall) origin rather than an intrapulmonary mass. This is confirmed by the CT images showing a large, encapsulated fluid-density collection in the right hemithorax consistent with a pleural effusion or cyst.
